httpd-mod-ssl-directive-config.quote:
SSLEngine
SSL Engine Operation Switch
Syntax: SSLEngine
httpd-mod-ssl-directive-config.reason: The span joins the directive name SSLEngine to its title line 'SSL Engine Operation Switch' and the following 'Syntax: SSLEngine' declaration across line breaks; all three are component identity and reference-page boilerplate (a directive name, its title, and its syntax label), not a prose noun pile a reader must parse.
'Context: server config, virtual host' is a labelled metadata field listing two established httpd configuration scopes, comma-separated; there is no ambiguous grouping for a reader to guess.
'Support ... was removed in 2.4.64' is descriptive release history, not an instruction; the actor (the httpd developers) is irrelevant and naming them would add nothing.

The only sensible referent for 'It enabled RFC 2817 support' is the 'optional' argument (or, equivalently, support for it); reading 'It' as the version 2.4.64 contradicts the same sentence, so the competing readings do not change the meaning.
'SSL/TLS Protocol Engine' is the capitalised component name mod_ssl uses for itself; component identity outranks simplification.
The bare 'This' parallels 'This directive' in the immediately preceding sentence, and only a directive can be 'used inside a VirtualHost section'; the engine and the usage do not fit the predicate.
Second occurrence of the established component name 'SSL/TLS Protocol Engine'; a real product/component name is never a noun-cluster defect.

httpd-mod-ssl-directive-config.quote:
SSLFIPS
SSL FIPS mode Switch
Syntax: SSLFIPS
httpd-mod-ssl-directive-config.reason: Same structural artefact as the SSLEngine heading: the directive name SSLFIPS joined across line breaks to its title 'SSL FIPS mode Switch' and its 'Syntax: SSLFIPS' declaration. Directive identity and reference-page boilerplate, not an opaque noun run.

'It must be set in the global server context' follows a sentence containing both 'This directive' and 'the SSL library FIPS_mode flag'; proximity favours the flag but the truth is the SSLFIPS directive, and the two readings tell the reader to configure different things.
The passive states a placement constraint on the directive (where it must appear), not an action assigned to an actor; who edits the configuration file is immaterial to the constraint.
'If httpd was compiled against an SSL library ...' is a descriptive condition about an existing build; whoever compiled httpd is genuinely unknown and naming an actor would be misleading.
'may be described as ...' is a careful compliance statement in descriptive prose where the describing party is deliberately unnamed; supplying an actor would change the claim.

'when all components are assembled and operated under the guidelines' is a compliance condition, not an instruction; the agent is intentionally generic because the condition holds regardless of who performs it.

sqlite-cli-description.reason: 'accepts user input and passes it down into the SQLite library' — 'it' is the direct object of the coordinated verb and can only be 'user input'; the other nouns are not candidates for being passed down.
'When somebody says ... they might be referring to' is the singular 'they' bound to 'somebody'; no competing referent is grammatically available.
'is written by and for the core SQLite developers' is descriptive and already names the agent; an active rewrite would break the 'by and for' coordination and lose meaning.
'Graphical User Interface (GUI)' is a standard term of art being formally introduced with its abbreviation; the run is conventional and unambiguous.

llvm-getting-started-build.reason: 'you can filter them from your git fetch' can only refer to the user branches named as the topic of the same sentence; nothing else in context is filterable from a fetch refspec.

llvm-standalone-build-table.reason: 'the original folder where LLVM was built' is a descriptive relative clause identifying a folder; the builder is the reader and is already obvious, and the sentence is about location, not about who acted.
'if llvm is installed into /usr/bin' is a conditional describing an existing installation state; how it got there and who installed it are irrelevant to the condition.
'options are required' is an adjectival predicate stating a requirement, not a passive verb with a suppressed actor.
'can be found in the table below' is a descriptive cross-reference, not an instruction; the sentence points at a table rather than assigning an action to anyone.
'build targets are supported for the sub-projects listed' describes a capability of the build system; there is no actor a reader needs to know.

zephyr-dependency-setup.reason: A reader groups this as [command-line] [Zephyr development environment]; the hyphenated modifier and the established product name 'Zephyr' fix the structure without guesswork.

'instructions for other Linux distributions are discussed in :ref:`installation_linux`' is a parenthetical cross-reference about the document itself, not part of the instruction; the agent is the documentation and is irrelevant.
